artworks.title: Achilles at the Court of Lycomedes
artworks.description: Batoni’s Uffizi canvas fills Lycomedes’ Skyrian palace with daughters and a disguised Achilles — the king’s court as the stage where Odysseus will unmask the hero. Neoclassical polish keeps Lycomedes the named host of the most painted episode of Achilles’ youth.

artworks.title: Achilles Discovered among the Daughters of Lycomedes
artworks.description: Lairesse’s Mauritshuis painting freezes the trumpet-and-weapons test in Lycomedes’ hall — Achilles seizing steel while the king’s daughters scatter. Dutch classicism made Skyros’ court the European image of the concealed hero.

artworks.title: Achilles among the Daughters of Lycomedes
artworks.description: Quellinus packs Lycomedes’ household into Flemish Baroque theatre — the Skyrian king’s daughters and the youth who will leave them for Troy. The title keeps Lycomedes the frame even when Achilles steals the eye.

artworks.title: Achilles and the Daughters of Lycomedes
artworks.description: Tiarini’s Bolognese canvas stages the same Skyrian recognition under Lycomedes’ roof — Italian Baroque light on the court that hid Achilles until the arms called him out.

popCulture.title: Lycomedes of Scyros
popCulture.description: King of Skyros who raised Achilles among his daughters — and, in some tellings, cast Theseus to his death from the island cliffs.
